audit.title: Data Streams Billing

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The opening sentence is self-contained and quotable, but it answers only "what billing model?" — not the dominant "how much?" intent. Adequate for what little it covers.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Single section, no H2/H3, no table, no bullets (measured: 1 heading, 0 tables, 0 bullets). Fine for 87 words, but there is nothing to chunk or extract as reasons.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 numerals, 0 units, no version/network detail. For a billing page this is the critical failure — no prices, tiers, verification limits, or currency.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 2 links, both to contact/typeform forms; 0 to primary sources. No link to a pricing spec, terms, or a canonical Data Streams overview.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "Chainlink Data Streams uses a subscription-based billing option" is liftable. The deprecation note is also crisply stated.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified. Head metadata could not be verified from served HTML — CLI should pass raw `<head>`. A billing page especially needs a visible last-updated signal.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code expected on a billing page; neutral.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "what is the billing model" and flags the deprecated pay-per-verification model, but misses "how much does it cost," "what networks are supported," "how do I subscribe," and any FAQ/troubleshooting.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clear and unambiguous; consistent use of "Chainlink Data Streams." Strong; minor issue is the leftover `{" "}` JSX artifact in the deprecation note.

audit.summary: This is an 87-word stub that tells the reader Data Streams uses a subscription-based billing model and directs everything else to a "contact us" form. Its one genuine strength is a clean, liftable opening claim ("Chainlink Data Streams uses a subscription-based billing option"). Its biggest opportunity is that a *billing* page contains zero concrete pricing facts — no prices, tiers, units, supported networks, or examples — so any generative engine asked "how much does Chainlink Data Streams cost?" cannot cite this page for an answer and will fall back on parametric priors or third-party sources. Honest verdict: content-starved; retrieval may work but there is almost nothing here to synthesize.

recommendations.title: Add concrete billing specifics
recommendations.issue: "Contact us to learn more about Mainnet pricing" — page has 0 numerals.
recommendations.change: Add whatever can be published: what a subscription meters (per-report, per-verification, monthly tier), supported networks/chains, currency/payment token, and any published limits. Even a small table (Item | What's billed | Notes) gives engines extractable facts.
recommendations.why: Quantitative billing facts are the single highest-lift change; a billing page with zero numbers cannot be cited for cost questions.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased headings
recommendations.where: replace the flat single section with H2s.
recommendations.issue: no headings match how users ask ("how much does Data Streams cost?").
recommendations.change: Add H2s such as "How much does Chainlink Data Streams cost?", "What billing model does Data Streams use?", "Is pay-per-verification still supported?", "How do I start a subscription?"
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` and canonical/last-updated
recommendations.issue: measured 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `dateModified`, a canonical URL, and a visible "Last updated" line. Deprecation notices make freshness signals especially valuable here.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and let engines date the deprecation claim.

recommendations.title: Make the deprecation a first-class, liftable statement
recommendations.issue: "The pay-per-verification billing model has been deprecated" buried in a callout with a JSX artifact `{" "}`.
recommendations.change: Surface a plain sentence: "As of [date], the pay-per-verification model is deprecated; Data Streams now bills via subscription only." Remove the `{" "}` artifact.
recommendations.why: A dated, self-contained deprecation claim prevents engines from confidently citing the old model from stale priors.

recommendations.title: Link to primary/canonical sources
recommendations.issue: both links are contact forms; 0 authoritative references.
recommendations.change: Add inline links to the Data Streams overview/architecture page and any published pricing or terms page, not only to the typeform.
recommendations.why: Internal links into a canonical hub raise credibility and help this thin page inherit retrieval authority.

antiPatterns: Wall-of-nothing stub: an entire page whose primary intent (cost) is deflected to a contact form.
JSX rendering artifact `{" "}` leaks into prose in the deprecation note.
Undated deprecation claim ("has been deprecated" with no date/version).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this billing URL is indexed there.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical injection and a freshness cadence for billing/deprecation pages are template-level fixes beyond this page.
Whether pricing can be published at all may be a business/legal constraint; if so, the page should still name what is billed even if not the dollar amounts.
